description: Our aim is to build a health monitoring software that gathers health indicators and enables astronauts to evaluate and act on the status of their health .
summary:
AHMS (Advanced Health Monitoring System) is a smart wrist-worn health monitoring device developed by Team G-Vitals to support astronaut and crew health awareness during demanding missions. It monitors important health and activity information, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂) and steps.

The project follows four stages: Wear → Drift → Alert → Decide. Once worn, the device monitors readings and identifies changes from an individual's normal baseline. When it detects a potentially concerning pattern, it generates alerts through vibration and sound while recording the event in a log. Its Run mode helps distinguish exercise-related increases in heart rate from other possible concerns, reducing unnecessary alerts.

The prototype uses a MAX30102 sensor, a MAX98357A speaker module, a vibration motor, a microphone and an interactive screen interface. It also supports touch controls, voice notes and event-history reviews.

Our goal is to help crew members recognise possible health changes earlier and make informed decisions. AHMS is designed to support human judgement, not replace medical professionals. By combining wearable technology, explainable alerts and human decision-making, we aim to contribute to safer and more informed space missions.
details:
Our project demonstration is an interactive digital prototype of the AHMS wrist device.

Live prototype: https://ahms-wrist-device.netlify.app/

The demonstration showcases:

- Live heart-rate and SpO₂ readings.
- Battery and step-count information.
- Simulated stress-related changes in vital signs.
- Audio and vibration alerts.
- Run mode to prevent unnecessary exercise-related heart-rate alarms.
- Touchscreen navigation and multiple device screens.
- Voice-note recording and event logging.

The demonstration shows the complete Wear → Drift → Alert → Decide process and explains how the device helps users understand health changes.
